findings.description: The try block also wraps self._flush(), so an exception from sink.write (I/O or DB error) is caught by `except Exception`. The whole batch of up to batch_size rows is dropped because `batch` was already reset to []. Only the single row that triggered the flush is reported as rejected, with the sink's error message. The load then continues and returns a report that looks mostly successful. Rows are lost silently and sink outages are treated like bad data.
findings.suggestion: Only wrap parse_row in the try/except, and call self._flush outside it so sink errors propagate. For example: try: tx = parse_row(row) except ValueError/parse error as exc: record rejection; continue; then batch.append(tx) and flush when full.
findings.title: Sink write failures are recorded as a rejection of the current row
